name: one_square
summary: The exchange theorem for (U₁ ⊕ U₂, A, A′) with polynomial real data; the constant κ is obtained by approximating its real datum by polynomial vectors (the integrals lie in a fixed line, closed); the equivariances of the two compositions give the first two laws of SquareLaw, and the partner identity is the exchange identity transported through Fubini and the adjointness of lift and descent.

steps.claim: Not a step of the proof: lines 65–70 are the rest of the statement, which ends before the `:=` on line 70 (a second-reader message). The line census takes the `:=` of `let u i x :=` on line 65 for the start of the value, so the check requires these lines to be owned here. They state: u(i, x) = modDescent(·, A, b(i), Φ₂, δ_{x₂}, ·, ·) ∘ modLift(U₁, A, a(i), Φ₁, δ_{x₁}, ·, k(¬d)), v(i, y) = modLift(A′, U₂, a(i), Φ₂′, δ_{y₂}, ·, k₂(¬d)) ∘ modDescent(·, ·, b(i), Φ₁′, δ_{y₁}, k₁(¬d), k′(¬d)), and: there are C, κ such that every i has c ≠ 0 with |c|² = C·lValueProd(places(𝔪(i)), ν(i), e) and SquareLaw(χ(i), σ, κ/c, x ↦ l(u(i, x)(f)), y ↦ l(v(i, y)(f))) for every f and every linear functional l.
steps.lean:
(ν i)⁻¹ (n₁ ⊕ n₂)) : let u i x := modDescent _ A (b i) Φ₂ (Pi.single x.toCols₂ 1) _ _ ∘ₗ modLift
                         U₁ A (a i) Φ₁ (Pi.single x.toCols₁ 1) _ (k !d)
  let v i y := modLift A' U₂ (a i) Φ₂' (Pi.single y.toRows₂ 1) _ (k₂ !d) ∘ₗ
    modDescent _ _ (b i) Φ₁' (Pi.single y.toRows₁ 1) (k₁ !d) (k' !d)
  ∃ C κ, ∀ i, ∃ c ≠ 0, ‖c‖ ^ 2 = C * lValueProd (𝔪 i).places (ν i) e ∧
    ∀ f (l : _ →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ), SquareLaw (χ i) σ (κ / c) (l <| u i · f) (l <| v i · f) := by

steps.claim: Introduce u, v. The exchange theorem for (U₁ ⊕ U₂, A, A′) (`exchange_theorem`, with hs, he, hn, hμ and a rapid polynomial vector): C, a rapid real datum x (h₀) and the identity H.
steps.lean:
intro u v; obtain ⟨C, _, h₀, H⟩ :=
    exchange_theorem (U₁.sum U₂) A A' σ hs he hn hμ (weightedNorm_polyVector_ne_top · _)

steps.claim: Integrable majorants: for every pair (f, f′) of forms on U₁, U₂ and every (i, x) with x having a left-invertible transpose, the kernel built from the lift by the point datum has an integrable bound (`exists_integrable_kernel_bound`; N, D, hi, hF), the theta kernel decaying for data named at the places of 𝔪(i) (`pairTheta_decay_of_onto`, `isPrimitiveMatrix_of_liftFn_ne_zero`).
steps.lean:
choose N D hi hF using fun j : (_ × U₂.Form (k₂ d)) × Σ i, {x // HasLeftInv (R :=
    (𝔪 i).ResRing) xᵀ} ↦ exists_integrable_kernel_bound (h₁.1.form_mem_rapidFunctions j.1.1)
    (h₂.1.form_mem_rapidFunctions j.1.2) (pairTheta_decay_of_onto _ A (rankTwist _ (n₁ ⊕ n₂)) 1
    (evalAt _) (𝔪 _).disjoint_places_star ((𝔪 _).isSchwartzBruhat_liftFn
    (Pi.single j.2.2.1 1 ∘ vecToMat)) (fun _ c ↦ (isPrimitiveMatrix_of_liftFn_ne_zero _ (by
    simpa using fun _ ↦ (· ▸ j.2.2.2)) (ht _).1.some.2 c).2.imp (by tauto)) 0)

steps.claim: x is a limit of polynomial vectors P_k in the weighted norms (`exists_tendsto_weightedNorm`), with integrable kernels (hp), and polynomial vectors are spanned by products of polynomials in the two groups of variables (`mem_rename_range_mul`; S).
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨⟨P, hP⟩, hp, S⟩ := exists_tendsto_weightedNorm h₀, (hi · _ <|
    weightedNorm_polyVector_ne_top _ ·), mem_rename_range_mul _ _

steps.claim: The vector of integrals j ↦ ∫ f′·u(·)(f) for the datum x is the limit of those for P_k (dominated by D·weightedNorm(x − P_k) → 0, hF); each of those lies in the line spanned by one fixed vector (shown below), which is closed (finite-dimensional), so the limit is κ times that vector (hκ); κ may be 0 (the closed span of one vector contains 0), and the same κ serves the whole family.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨C, ((LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ _ fun j ↦ ∫ g, j.1.2 g * u _ j.2.2.1 j.1.1 g
    ∂U₂.quotMeasure).range.closed_of_finiteDimensional.isSeqClosed (fun n ↦ ?_) (tendsto_pi_nhds.2
    fun j ↦ tendsto_sub_nhds_zero_iff.1 (squeeze_zero_norm' (((hP _).eventually_ne bot_ne_top).mono
    fun n h ↦ integral_sub (hp j (P n)) (by tauto) ▸ norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const <| .of_forall
    (hF j _ h · |>.trans_eq' <| by rw [norm_sub_rev]; simp [mul_sub])) ((((ENNReal.tendsto_toReal
    bot_ne_top).comp (hP _)).const_smul_zero (D j)).zero_smul_const _)))).imp fun κ hκ i ↦ ?_⟩

steps.claim: For each P_k: induction over products of polynomials (`Submodule.mul_induction_on`); sums are handled by the additivity of the integrals.
steps.lean:
refine Submodule.mul_induction_on (S ?x (P n)) ?_ fun P Q ↦ (Set.mem_of_eq_of_mem
    (by ext; simpa [mul_add] using integral_add (hp ..) (hp ..)) <| add_mem · ·)

steps.claim: Treat a product P·Q of polynomials in the two groups of variables.
steps.lean: swap; rintro _ ⟨P, rfl⟩ _ ⟨Q, rfl⟩

steps.claim: The lifts by P and by Q are real convolutions (`IsEdgeFamily.exists_lift_eq_realConv`: α, β).
steps.lean: obtain ⟨⟨α, e₁⟩, β, e₂⟩ := h₁.exists_lift_eq_realConv P, h₂.exists_lift_eq_realConv Q

steps.claim: For forms F, F′ the Petersson product of the two real convolutions is an integral identity e (`petersson_realConv_realConv`).
steps.lean:
have e F (F' : A.Form _) := by
    simpa [petersson, realConv, ← integral_conj] using (conjForm (eq_star_of_eq_star (h₂.2.1 d).2)
      F).2.petersson_realConv_realConv (h₁.2.1 _).1 F'.2 (star α).integrable β.integrable

steps.claim: The integral for P·Q factors, by Fubini (`MeasureTheory.integral_prod_symm`), into the Petersson pairing of the two convolutions, which by e and the adjointness of lift and descent through the arrow of h₂ (`IsArrow.integral_mul_formLift_swap`) is the integral of the composite descent ∘ lift: a fixed vector times a scalar, as required.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨_, funext fun _ ↦ ((integral_prod_symm _ (hp ..)).trans (.trans ?_ ((e ..).trans (congrArg
    _ (h₂.isArrow_modDatum.elim (·.integral_mul_formLift_swap · ..)))))).symm⟩

steps.claim: Rewrite with the convolutions and the integrals of products.
steps.lean: simp_rw [← realConv.eq_1, ← e₁, ← e₂, lift, ← integral_prod_mul]

steps.claim: Identify the kernels: the theta kernel of the data with point functions is modKernel summed over the left factor (`modKernel_sum_left`), with a(i)·b(i) = rankTwist(ν(i)⁻¹) (hE).
steps.lean:
congr! 4; erw [← modKernel, (?_ : Pi.single _ _ = _), ← hE _ rfl,
    modKernel_sum_left]; simp [field]

steps.claim: The block identity for the point function: (fromCols of the column blocks).
steps.lean: grind [fromCols_toCols]

steps.claim: The remaining simple goal.
steps.lean: simp

steps.claim: For an index i: from H for (𝔪(i), ν(i), χ(i)) (ht): c ≠ 0 (c₀), |c|² = C·lValueProd (c₁) and the exchange identity H; the character identities e (from hE) and o (the cardinality through σ); and t, the relations of the tame characters (inverse and product with υ).
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨⟨c, c₀, c₁, H⟩, e, o, t⟩ := H _ _ _ (ht i), (mul_comm ..).trans (hE i (add_comm ..)), by
    simpa using card_congr σ,
    (((ht i).inv.mul (hasWeight_upsilonU1_pow _)).inv (ν := rankTwist _ (n₁ ⊕ n₂)))

steps.claim: Take c with these properties; the square law: (1) translating the point datum of u by k ∈ GL changes the lift and the descent by elements of the level, which multiply the forms by χ(det k) (`IsArrow.formRep_formLift_of_eq_smul`, `pairWeil_modDatum_single`, `apply_eq_mul_of_formRep_one`, `IsTameFor.apply_det`); (2) the same for v on the right; (3) the partner identity remains.
steps.lean:
use c, c₀, c₁, fun f l ↦ ⟨fun u x ↦ apply_eq_mul_of_formRep_one
    (h₁.isArrow_modDatum.1.formRep_formLift_of_eq_smul (pairWeil_modDatum_single 1 _) _)
    (h₂.isArrow_modDatum.2.formRep_formLift_of_eq_smul (pairWeil_modDatum_single 1 (liftMod u)⁻¹) _)
    (by simpa [← hE i rfl, ← map_inv] using t.apply_det (liftMod u)), fun u x ↦
    apply_eq_mul_of_formRep_one
    (h₄.isArrow_modDatum.2.formRep_formLift_of_eq_smul (pairWeil_modDatum_single (liftMod u) 1) _)
    (h₃.isArrow_modDatum.1.formRep_formLift_of_eq_smul (pairWeil_modDatum_single _ 1) _)
    (by simpa [← e] using t.apply_det (liftMod u)), fun Φ Ψ hP ↦ ?_⟩

steps.claim: Move the scalars and sums inside l.
steps.lean: simp only [← smul_eq_mul, ← map_smul, ← map_sum]

steps.claim: It suffices to compare the inner products with every z (`ext_inner_left`); let f′ be the conjugate form of z.
steps.lean: refine congrArg l (ext_inner_left ℂ fun z ↦ ?_); let f' := conjForm (d.not_not ▸ (h₂.1 _).2) z

obtain ⟨L, R, K⟩ := fun x ↦ integral_integral_sum_eq fun y hy ↦ (⟨·, integral_prod_symm _ ‹_›⟩)
    ((exists_integrable_kernel_bound (h₁.1.form_mem_rapidFunctions f) (h₂.1.form_mem_rapidFunctions
    f') (pairTheta_modDatum_decay A' _ x x (Ψ := Pi.single y 1) (ht i).1 (by simpa using ⟨_,
    (hP.2 y hy).choose_spec.2 ▸ invFirstRows_mul_firstCols ..⟩) 0)).choose_spec.choose_spec _
    (weightedNorm_polyVector_ne_top _ _)).1, integral_integral_sum_eq fun x hx ↦ by
    simpa +instances only using (fun j ↦ (⟨hi j _ (h₀ _), congr($hκ j).symm⟩ : _ ∧ _ = κ * _)) ⟨(f,
      f'), i, x, (hP.1 x hx).choose_spec.2 ▸ hasLeftInv_invLastRows_transpose ..⟩, by
    simpa only [thetaIntegral, pairTheta, modDatum_eq_sum _ _ Φ, modDatum_eq_sum _ _ Ψ, map_sum,
      map_smul] using H Φ Ψ hP
